DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 130 s. 2022 October 17, 2022 HON. GLORIA MONTENEGRO-CONSTANTINO Municipal Mayor Abra, de Ilog, Occidental Mindoro Dear Mayor Montenegro-Constantino: This pertains to your letter dated 29 July 2022 concerning a boundary dispute between Abra de Ilog Occidental Mindoro and Puerto Galera, Oriental Mindoro. The antecedent facts are as follows: I. The issue has been subject of joint hearings between the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of both provinces of Occidental Mindoro and Oriental Mindoro; and 2. The evidences for both have been presented and admitted by the DILG as the sitting adjudicator. The request is for the Department "to exercise its mandate of resolving boundary disputes between provinces, leaving the courts as the last and painstaking resort in sorting out this issue". Please be informed that resolving boundary disputes is not within the mandate of this Department as the jurisdictional responsibility thereon belongs to the concerned Sanggunian/s as explicitly dictated by Section 118, Chapter 1, Title Nine, Book l, of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", viz: "SECTION 118. Jurisdictional Responsibility for Settlement of Boundary Dispute. - Boundary disputes between and among local government units shall, as much as possible, be settled amicably. To this end: (a) Boundary disputes involving two (2) or more Barangays in the same city or municipality shall be referred for settlement to the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang bayan concerned. (b) Boundary disputes involving two (2) or more municipalities within the same province shall be referred for settlement to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan concerned. (c) Boundary disputes involving municipalities or component cities of different provinces shall be jointly referred for settlement to the Sanggunians of the provinces concerned. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

(d) Boundary disputes involving a component city or municipality on the one hand and a highly urbanized city on the other, or two (2) or more highly urbanized cities, shall be jointly referred for settlement to the respective Sanggunians of the parties. (e) In the event the Sanggunian fails to effect an amicable settlement within sixty (60) days from the date the dispute was referred thereto, it shall issue a certification to that effect. Thereafter, the dispute shall be formally tried by the Sanggunian concerned which shall decide the issue within sixty (60) days from the date of the certification referred to above." (Emphasis Supplied) A representative of this Department, per your submission in the letter-request, may have assisted in the capacity of an adjudicator. That is permissible but only in an attempt to amicably settle the boundary dispute, the very first stage in the settlement procedure. In the event of failure to effect an amicable settlement, a formal trial shall proceed before the Sanggunian/s concerned. On this, subsections (e) and (c) shall become operative, insofar as dispute between municipalities/cities of different provinces is concerned. The decision of the Sanggunian/s concerned in the boundary dispute is not appealable, nor subject to a Motion for Reconsideration, before this Department. That is in view of an express provision thereon under Section 119, Chapter I, Title Nine, Book l, of the Local Government Code, viz: SECTION 119. Appeal. - Within the time and manner prescribed by the Rules of Court, any party may elevate the decision of the Sanggunian concerned to the proper Regional Trial Court having jurisdiction over the area in dispute. The Regional Trial Court shall decide the appeal within one (1) year from the filing thereof. Pending final resolution of the disputed area prior to the dispute shall be maintained and continued for all legal purposes. As to the detailed procedure in the settlement of boundary dispute, may we direct attention to Articles 17 and 18, Rule 3, Of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Local Government Code. The same is cited in DILG Opinion No. 81 s. 2021. Notwithstanding, this opinion is being issued without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of more competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, Authority of the Secretary: B JUAN VICTOR R. LLAMAS n rsecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs opy Furnished: DIR. KARL CAESAR RIMANDO DILG Regional Office IV-B MIMAROPA Page 2 of 2
